questions.q: Why is it inaccurate to describe Chapter 7's discrepancy as an unplanned detour from this capstone's real work?
options: Because Chapter 7 was actually scripted from the very beginning of the course
Because catching exactly this kind of error was the entire reason three independent front-ends were built on one shared warehouse instead of one dashboard shown three ways
Because Chapter 7 doesn't actually involve any real data
Because the warehouse was rebuilt from scratch in Chapter 7
questions.explain: The architecture's whole value proposition was proven, not interrupted, by Chapter 7 — three independent paths to a number existed specifically so they could disagree and reveal a real error.

questions.q: Which six layers does this capstone's full build actually include, across Chapters 2 through 7?
options: Only a Power BI dashboard and an Excel workbook
A T-SQL warehouse, a Python validation layer, a Power BI front-end, a Tableau front-end, an Excel front-end, and the cross-tool discrepancy investigation
Four separate copies of the same dashboard in four different tools
A single SQL view and three identical PDF exports
questions.explain: Each of these six pieces was built for real — a T-SQL warehouse, automated Python validation, and three independent front-ends, with the discrepancy investigation testing all of them together.

questions.q: How does this Advanced capstone relate to the Beginner and Intermediate tiers of the same Data Analyst → BI Engineer path?
options: It is completely unrelated and uses a different fictional company
It is the third and final tier for the same fictional company, Thornbury Cycle Supply Co., operating at a larger scale with multiple tools and an automated validation layer
It replaces the Beginner and Intermediate tiers entirely
It is an optional elective with no connection to the rest of the path
questions.explain: All three tiers build on the same company and scenario, with this Advanced tier reaching the scale and cross-functional complexity closest to a real BI engineer's actual role.

questions.q: Which of the following is named as a real, deliberately out-of-scope extension a genuinely senior version of this project might add next?
options: Automated reconciliation that checks all three tools' totals on a schedule and alerts on any gap above a small tolerance
Removing the warehouse entirely and connecting all three tools directly to raw AdventureWorks2012 tables
Deleting Finance's Excel workbook since Power BI and Tableau already agree
Combining all three front-ends into a single tool with no independent checks
questions.explain: Automated reconciliation, row-level lineage, and a formal change-management process are all named as deliberate, honest scope boundaries this capstone didn't cross — not as mistakes.

questions.q: What is the single most important thing this capstone demonstrated about why it was built the way it was?
options: That Tableau is a better tool than Power BI for all use cases
That a shared source of truth with independently-built front-ends can catch a real, specific error before it reaches a board meeting — which it visibly did in Chapter 7
That Excel should never be used for business reporting
That data warehouses are unnecessary if the front-end tools are well built
questions.explain: The entire architecture's purpose was proven concretely: the discrepancy was caught and corrected specifically because three independent paths to the same number existed to disagree.
